s: Which of the following longitude is called as international date line?
There is a Place-A with longitude 06° West. There is another Place-B with longitude 09° East. If the local time at Place-A is 10 AM, what would be the local time at Place-B ?
x: The 15° difference between 6°W and 9°E equals 1 hour at 15° per hour, and the eastern place is ahead, so the time at Place-B is 11 AM.

s: There is a place A with longitude 060° West. There is another place B with longitude 090° East. If the local time at place A is 10 a.m., what would be the local time at place B?
x: The longitude difference is 150°, i.e. 10 hours at 15° per hour. As the eastern place is ahead, 10 AM at 60°W is 8 PM at 90°E.

s: If the earth's direction of rotation is reversed, what would be the IST when it is noon at the International Date Line?
x: Normally, the Earth rotates from west to east, so places in the east are ahead in time. IST (82.5° E) is therefore 6 hours 30 minutes behind the International Date Line (180°). If the Earth's direction of rotation were reversed, time calculation would also reverse, and places to the west would become ahead in time. Since IST lies west of the Physical Geography PMF IAS Geo – 39 International Date Line by 97.5° longitude, IST would be 6 hours 30 minutes ahead of it. Therefore, when it is 12:00 noon at the International Date Line, IST would be 18:30 hrs (6:30 PM).

s: When there is noon at G.M.T. meridian, people at another place on the Earth are taking their 6 o'clock morning tea. The longitude of the place is
x: When it is 12:00 noon at the Greenwich meridian (GMT), a place that is 6 hours behind will show 6:00 AM. Since the Earth rotates 360° in 24 hours, it covers 15° of longitude per hour (or 1° in 4 minutes). Thus, a 1-hour time difference equals 15° of longitude. A 6-hour difference corresponds to 6 × 15° = 90°. Because the local time is earlier than GMT, the location lies to the west of Greenwich — at 90° W longitude.

s: When it is noon along 820 30' E longitude along what degree of longitude it will be 6.30 a.m.?
x: When there is a midday at 82030' E longitude then 6:30 in the morning means there is a difference of 5:30 hrs in time. As in one hour the change in longitude is 150 therefore 820 30' difference in 5:30 hours is 820 30' – 820 30' = 00 latitude.

s: If the Sun rises at TIRAP in Arunachal Pradesh at 5.00 am (IST) then what time (IST) will the Sun rise in Kandla in Gujarat?
x: There is a difference of about 2 hours between Kandla (Gujarat) and Tirap (Arunachal Pradesh) due to the longitudinal position of both the cities. Thus, if the Sun rises at Tirap (95° 31') in Arunachal Pradesh at 5:00 a.m. (IST), then the Sun will rise at 7:00 a.m. in Kandla (70° 11').

s: The time at Cairo is 2 hours ahead of Greenwich. Hence, it is located at-
x: Cairo (Egypt) is located at 300 3'N latitude and 310 14' E longitude. The time of Cairo is 2 hours ahead of Greenwich. Therefore its position approximately falls near the 300 East longitude. The Earth being spherical in shape rotates on its axis by 3600 in 24 hours. Therefore, its movement for 10 of longitude takes the time of 4 minutes. So, it can be easily calculated that in 120 minutes ( 2 hours) the angle for longitude will be 300 , Therefore, option (b) should be the correct answer.

s: When it is midnight at IST meridian, a place observes 6 A.M. The meridian on which the said place is located is-
x: When there is midnight at the IST meridian, a place that observes 6:00 A.M. has to be in the east of India. It is because the Sun rises early in the east. The difference in their meridian after 6 hours will be 15 × 6 = 90º (15º = 1 hour). Indian Standard Time (IST) is the time observed throughout India and is 0 calculated based on the 821 2 East longitude. Thus, the 0 place is situated at = 90º + 821 2 = 172º 30' East.

s: The local time of a place is 6:00 AM when the Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) is 3:00 AM, what is the longitude of the place ?
x: Greenwich Mean Time (G.M.T.) is referred to as Coordinated Universal Time (U.T.C.). International time is calculated from Greenwich at the 0 Meridian, and the time eastward of it is while the time westward of it is behind (although dates are measured from the 1800 meridian at the International Date Line which passes through the mid of the Pacific Ocean). Meridians situated 1800 east of Greenwich are called East-meridians and meridians situated at 1800 west are known as West-meridians. All the meridians in 3600 of the globe are divided into 24 time zones (150 – 150 meridian difference). Therefore, each time zone has a 1 hour time difference and each meridian has the difference of 4 minutes, moving each meridian east G.M.T. time is 4 minutes ahead and moving west of G.M.T. time remains 4 minutes behind for each meridian. According to the question time is to be calculated for that place which is ahead (6-3=3 hrs) of Greenwich. As we know for 1 hours difference in longitude (meridian) is 150 therefore for 3 hours the difference will be 15 × 3 = 450 , So that place will lie at 450 east of Greenwich.

s: What is the local time of Thimphu (Bhutan) located at 900 East longitude when the time at Greenwich (00) is 12:00 noon :
x: Difference between Greenwich and Thimphu (Bhutan) = 900 of longitudes Total time difference = 90 × 4 = 360 minutes ∴ The time increases at a rate of 4 minutes per one degree of longitude. = 360 / 60 hours = 6 hour = 6 hours / Local time of Thimphu is 6 hours more than that at Greenwich i.e. 6.00 p.m.

s: Captain of a ship moving Westward records the local time of 10-00 hrs Monday at 90o W. If the speed of the ship is the same as the speed of the rotation of the earth, which of the following local time and day would be found by the captain at International date line:
x: Captain of the ship traveling westward recorded the local time 10:00 hours at 900 west Meridian, this means that the ship is near the North American continent. Since the Earth rotates from west to east on its axis (anticlockwise) and the ship is moving towards west with the speed equivalent to the Earth’s rotation therefore, both are moving in opposite directions but there is no effect of Earth’s rotation upon the movement of objects upon its surface. So, for the ship covering 900 meridian it requires the time of 6 hours and the ship will be behind 6 hours according to local time. Therefore, when reaching the International Date Line he will write the local time as the same 10:00 hrs Monday. However, when he crosses the International Date Line his local time will be 10:00 hours Tuesday.

s: When there is noon at I.S.T. meridian people another place of the Earth is taking their 6 O'clock morning tea. The longitude of the place is :
x: The Earth makes one rotation (3600) in 24 hours, which means it passes through 150 in an hour from West to East. Every 150 we go Westward, local time becomes 1 hour behind the place, given in the question, which is 6:00 hours behind the I.S.T. (82030'E). So it is situated to the west of the I.S.T. 6:00 hour difference is equal to 900 longitudes (15×6 = 90). Thus, the place is situated at 900 west with respect to I.S.T. This gives the longitude of the place (with respect to Greenwich) as 7030' W (820.30' E-900=7030'W).

s: If the earth's direction of rotation is reversed, what should be the IST when it is noon at the International Date Line?

s: A telegram was sent from Greenwich at 12.00 Noon. The time for transmission was 12 minutes. It reached a town at 6.00 p.m. The longitude of the town will be :
x: Earth rotates on its axis in 24 hours and therefore completes the angle of 3600 in one rotation (i.e. 150 in an hour or 10 in 4 minutes). As the telegram sent from Greenwich at 12:00 noon reached another city at 6:00 evening and 12 minutes passed in messaging the telegram. The, total time = 6 hours – 12 minutes = 360 minutes – 12 minutes = 348 minutes. As we know for 60 minutes = 150 longitude for 348 minutes = 15 × 348/600 = 870 This is now clear that place where the telegram reached at 6:00 evening will be at 870 East longitude.

s: If it is 10.00 a.m. IST, then what would be the local time at Shillong at 92° E longitude?
x: Indian Standard Time is calculated on the basis of 82.5° E longitude .The difference between the longitude of Shillong and the Indian Standard Time is 92°-82.5° = 9.5° . As we know that the difference of 1 longitude is equal to 4 minutes. So the difference in time between them is 9.5 × 4 = 38 minutes. So, if a watch indicates 10:00 a.m. on IST , then 10:38 a.m. would be the local time at Shillong. Thus the correct answer is option (b).
